title: CLIWOC logbook tracks
notes: This is a small seed, not a complete atlas. Pre-1500 and most early-modern tracks are historical reconstructions with a citation each. The only logbook track is the CLIWOC LAUNCESTON cruise of 1769. DAS contributes two real voyage records; their paths are reconstructed. The full CLIWOC and DAS corpora were not drawn.

routes.notes: Daily positions taken unchanged from the downloaded CLIWOC cruise file (32 position days, 7 Sep–8 Oct 1769, 5th-rate frigate Launceston, Royal Navy, Halifax to Plymouth). This is a sample of CLIWOC 2.1 (287,114 records). The full database was not downloaded.

vessel.name: HMS Launceston
vessel.history: HMS Launceston was a 44-gun fifth rate in service from 1741 to 1784. In May 1745, under Captain Calmady, she was one of the ships at the capture of the French 64-gun Vigilant off Louisbourg during King George's War.
vessel.story: In September–October 1769 she sailed from Halifax to Plymouth, and her logbook recorded 32 noon positions. Those are the positions SeaGlobe draws.

routes.history: This is the only track in SeaGlobe drawn from real logged positions. It shows 32 daily noon positions of HMS Launceston between Halifax and Plymouth, 7 September – 8 October 1769, from the ship's logbook (National Maritime Museum, ADM/L/L53), digitised by the CLIWOC climate project. Launceston was a 44-gun fifth rate in Royal Navy service from 1741 to 1784.
routes.story: Each noon the officer of the watch wrote down the ship's position, wind and weather. More than 250 years later, climate scientists used those entries to rebuild the Atlantic weather of 1769, and SeaGlobe uses the same entries to draw the ship's track.
